title: The Entangled Condition
prompt:
**Scenario.** Count subsets S with (sum of S) divisible by 3 AND |S| even. Why does a per-element contribution flip fail here?

**Which approach is the best fit? The program only needs to print the letter.**

**A)** It doesn't fail — sums and parities are always separable

**B)** The two conditions interact through the same elements: an element's effect on parity and on sum-mod-3 cannot be counted independently of the set's other members, so the joint condition resists a single per-element split

**C)** Because 3 is prime

**D)** Because subsets can be empty

tests.name: answer
tests.hint: Joint conditions on overlapping statistics (sum mod 3 × count mod 2) need a joint state DP (position × sum%3 × parity), not a separable contribution flip. Knowing when NOT to flip is the skill.
